searches.reason: Translate qualitative feedback into evidence-grounded probes of redundancy, specific relevance, and compatibility. Seek methods for constructing auditable contrast sets from public titles, descriptions, and histories, with explicit supported, contradicted, and unknown labels. Missing specifications must remain unknown; purchase history cannot establish ownership or a fulfilled need. Validate probe labels against the available feedback from twenty users, reporting coverage and disagreement without inferring simulator traits.

searches.reason: Strong separation of sampled training pairs may conceal competition among plausible recommendations. Seek diagnostics that score the same HSTU model against fixed diagnostic candidate sets containing textually similar and popularity-matched unseen items, treating these as unobserved candidates rather than confirmed negatives. Examine positive ranks, top-list redundancy, and embedding hubness by training-frequency strata. Keep these descriptive measurements separate from the unchanged host validation HR@10 and avoid adding separately fitted scores to inference.

searches.reason: Move beyond aggregate deletion sensitivity to identify which HSTU components transmit historical information. Seek paired activation patching and gradient verification methods for gated attention, residual paths, and position embeddings, using histories matched on their final item but differing in earlier context. Require identity controls and agreement between attribution and measured interventions; report sensitivity without claiming causal user preferences. These probes should inspect the existing single model, preserve final-nonpadding readout, and generate a small predeclared set of training hypotheses.
